questions.question: Low-speed crashes:

options.text: Happen frequently, so there is no need to worry about them.

questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen at speeds under 30 miles per hour. Even low-speed crashes can kill you.

questions.question: For the best protection, riding gloves should be made of:
questions.explanation: Gloves should be made of leather or another tough material to protect your hands.

questions.question: If you drink alcohol, you should:

options.text: Decide if you can still ride safely based on how you feel.
Set a drinking limit so you can still ride safely.
Not worry about riding if you feel fine.

questions.explanation: The safest choice is to not ride after drinking. Any amount of alcohol can impair your ability to ride safely.

questions.question: Which of the following does not need to be checked regularly?
questions.explanation: Before every ride, check your tires, controls, chains, sprockets, shock absorbers, fasteners, and brakes. Small mechanical problems can be very dangerous on a motorcycle.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle on a slippery surface, you should:
questions.explanation: Slow down when riding on slippery surfaces. Use both brakes when stopping and avoid sudden movements.

questions.question: ____ can remove alcohol from your body.
questions.explanation: Only time can reduce your blood alcohol level. Coffee, exercise, fresh air, and cold showers cannot lower your blood alcohol or make you sober, though they may help you stay awake.

questions.question: Can clothing help prevent injuries in a crash?

options.text: No, clothing does not protect you.
No, clothing is just a personal choice.
Yes, but only if garments are very loose and flap in the wind.
Yes, if pants and a jacket cover your arms and legs.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, if pants and a jacket cover your arms and legs.
questions.explanation: Good clothing reduces crash injuries. Wear a jacket and pants that cover your arms and legs, are made of sturdy material, and fit snugly so they do not flap in the wind.

questions.question: Which of the following should you inspect before riding?

options.text: The wear and tread of your tires
The amount of cushion your seat has

questions.correctAnswerText: The wear and tread of your tires
questions.explanation: Before every ride, check your tires, oil and fluid levels, headlight, tail light, turn signals, brake light, clutch and throttle, mirrors, brakes, and horn.

questions.question: Mirror checks:

options.text: Should be part of your normal scanning routine.
Should be avoided because they will distract you.
Should be avoided since other drivers will see you easily.
Are only recommended in bad weather.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should be part of your normal scanning routine.
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors often to know what is behind you. Frequent mirror checks should be part of your normal scanning routine.

questions.question: Keep extra space between your motorcycle and the vehicle in front of you:

options.text: When stopping will be harder than usual.
When you want to look at the scenery.
To encourage other drivers to cut you off.
To prevent the driver in front of you from knowing you are there.

questions.correctAnswerText: When stopping will be harder than usual.
questions.explanation: Keep extra following distance when your motorcycle will need more time to stop. This includes slippery roads, when you cannot see ahead clearly, or when traffic is heavy.

questions.question: Most crashes happen in daylight. To be more visible, you should:
questions.explanation: Since most crashes happen in daylight, always wear bright-colored clothing while riding, even during the day.

questions.question: Goggles:

options.text: Protect your eyes, but not the rest of your face.
Protect your face, but not your eyes.
Do not protect your eyes as well as eyeglasses.

questions.correctAnswerText: Protect your eyes, but not the rest of your face.
questions.explanation: Goggles protect your eyes. Only a face shield protects your entire face. Eyeglasses are not a good replacement for goggles or a face shield.

questions.question: Before riding, check that:

options.text: The brakes make a loud squeaking noise.
The brakes cause friction with the steering.
Each brake can hold the motorcycle.
Only the rear brake can hold the motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Each brake can hold the motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Check each brake lever before every ride. Make sure each one feels firm and holds the motorcycle when fully applied.

questions.question: If you borrow a motorcycle:

options.text: Do not worry about checking the tire pressure.
Expect it to handle the same as your own bike.
The lender will check the brakes so you don't have to.
Keep extra space between you and other vehicles to give yourself more time to react.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep extra space between you and other vehicles to give yourself more time to react.
questions.explanation: Do the same safety checks on a borrowed motorcycle as you would on your own. Ride carefully with an unfamiliar motorcycle and allow extra stopping distance.

questions.question: A motorcycle has the best traction on:
questions.explanation: Many surfaces reduce traction. Wet pavement, gravel, sand, mud, snow, ice, painted lines, and metal plates are more dangerous than dry pavement.

questions.question: A motorcycle fits you if:

options.text: You can touch your feet to the ground while seated.
You can reach the controls by stretching.
The handlebars go over your head.
Your feet cannot rest on the foot pegs.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can touch your feet to the ground while seated.
questions.explanation: A motorcycle fits you correctly if your feet can reach the ground while seated. You should be able to reach and operate the controls easily.

questions.question: When checking tires before a ride, check all of the following except:
questions.explanation: Before each ride, check the air pressure, tread depth, and general wear of your tires.

questions.question: What reduces the risk of head or neck injury in a crash?

options.text: Not allowing a passenger on the motorcycle

questions.explanation: Wearing a helmet is the most effective way to reduce head and neck injuries in a crash.

questions.question: Which clothing helps other drivers see you?
questions.explanation: Wear gear that helps you and your motorcycle be spotted by others. Bright, reflective clothing makes it easier for other drivers to see you.

questions.question: Riding at night is usually:

options.text: Easier than riding during the day because you can see other vehicle lights better.
More difficult than riding during the day because visibility is worse.
Less distracting than riding during the day.

questions.correctAnswerText: More difficult than riding during the day because visibility is worse.
questions.explanation: Night riding is harder because you cannot see as well and others cannot see you. Without natural light and shadows, it is harder to judge distances.
